messages.title: The Database Committed. Where Is Event E?
messages.subtitle: Order42 is CONFIRMED in PostgreSQL, but the process crashed before publishing Event E. What durable publication obligation survived?
messages.property: If Order42 becomes authoritatively CONFIRMED, a durable publication obligation for Event E must also exist.
messages.takeaway: The outbox does not make the database and broker one transaction. It makes the publication obligation survive the business commit.
messages.challenge.title: What survived the crash?
messages.challenge.intro: The service committed Order42 = CONFIRMED in PostgreSQL, then crashed before invoking broker.Publish(E). No outbox record or other durable publication obligation was written.
messages.challenge.question: Does the current architecture guarantee that Event E can still be published?
messages.option.yes: Yes. A successful database commit includes broker publication.
messages.option.no: No. The business fact is durable, but the publication obligation is missing.
messages.option.needMore: We need to know which facts share a durability boundary.
messages.challenge.feedback: The database and broker are separate durability domains. A crash after the database commit but before Publish leaves Order42 CONFIRMED with neither Event E at the broker nor a durable obligation to publish it. Persisting an outbox record in the same database transaction closes this gap.
messages.deepDive.title: What does the outbox establish?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: A shared database transaction
messages.deepDive.section1.body: Update Order42 and insert Outbox E=PENDING in one authoritative database transaction. If it commits, both facts survive; if it rolls back, neither does.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: The relay can crash after publishing
messages.deepDive.section2.body: The broker may accept E while the relay crashes before recording E=SENT. After restart, E remains PENDING and the relay may publish again. Duplicate delivery is possible even though the original publication-obligation property holds.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: Marking SENT first trades one gap for another
messages.deepDive.section3.body: If the relay marks E=SENT before publishing, a crash between those actions can leave E unpublished with no pending obligation. Reversing the order does not make the database and broker atomic.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Transfer: a welcome email
messages.deepDive.section4.body: If AccountCreated is committed before WelcomeEmailRequested is queued, a crash can leave an account without a durable email obligation. Identify an authoritative storage boundary that can commit both facts together.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: When a separate outbox is unnecessary
messages.deepDive.section5.body: If authoritative business state and event append already commit atomically in one required storage boundary, a separate application outbox may add no protection. Determine which facts share the durability guarantee you need; do not prescribe an outbox table universally.

messages.rail.propertyHidden: The required durable publication obligation is not established yet.
messages.rail.evidenceGap: Order42 is CONFIRMED; the process crashed before publishing E.

messages.anchor.split-dual-write: Split database commit and broker publish
messages.anchor.durable-publication-intent: Durable publication intent in one DB transaction
messages.recap.2: Weak execution: the process crashes before a durable publication obligation exists.
messages.recap.3: Property: a CONFIRMED Order42 must have a durable obligation to publish E.
messages.recap.4: Enforcement: the same database transaction commits order state and Outbox E.

messages.step.review.title: Two successful-looking statements
messages.step.review.lead: The service marks Order42 CONFIRMED in PostgreSQL, then calls broker.Publish(E). The two statements look sequential, but they do not share a durability boundary.
messages.step.db-commit.title: The database returns success
messages.step.db-commit.lead: The database commits Order42 = CONFIRMED and returns success. Event E has not yet become durable at the broker.
messages.step.crash-gap.title: The process disappears
messages.step.crash-gap.lead: The process crashes before Publish(E) is invoked. The database commit survives; the process's unwritten intention does not.
messages.step.durable-question.title: What survives this point?
messages.step.durable-question.lead: Ask what survives if the process disappears now. Order42 is CONFIRMED, but no durable record requires Event E to be published.
messages.step.domains.title: See the durability boundary
messages.step.domains.lead: PostgreSQL and the message broker are separate durability domains. A successful database commit cannot by itself establish a broker fact.
messages.step.property.title: Name the obligation
messages.step.property.lead: If Order42 becomes authoritatively CONFIRMED, a durable publication obligation for Event E must also exist. E need not already be delivered.
messages.step.counterexample.title: The weak architecture violates it
messages.step.counterexample.lead: The database commits, the process crashes, and Publish(E) is never invoked. Order42 is CONFIRMED, but Event E and its durable publication obligation are absent.
messages.step.durable-intent.title: Commit intent with business state
messages.step.durable-intent.lead: Write Order42 = CONFIRMED and Outbox E = PENDING in one database transaction. The publication intent now survives the same commit as the business fact.
messages.step.repaired-domain.title: The broker is still separate
messages.step.repaired-domain.lead: The order state and Outbox E share the PostgreSQL commit boundary. The broker remains outside it; the outbox does not create a database-broker transaction.
messages.step.rollback.title: Rollback is also a positive control
messages.step.rollback.lead: If the database transaction rolls back, neither Order42 = CONFIRMED nor Outbox E becomes durable. The two facts move together.
messages.step.relay.title: Normal publication progresses
messages.step.relay.lead: The relay reads E=PENDING, publishes E, the broker accepts it, and the relay records completion. Valid progress remains possible.
messages.step.relay-crash.title: Move to the next crash boundary
messages.step.relay-crash.lead: The broker accepts E, but the relay crashes before recording E=SENT. The outbox row still says PENDING after restart.
messages.step.duplicates.title: Publication may repeat
messages.step.duplicates.lead: The relay may publish E again, so the broker may receive E twice. This is a remaining delivery boundary, not a failure of the original obligation property.
messages.step.property-preserved.title: Do not call the repair a failure
messages.step.property-preserved.lead: The original property remains preserved: a durable obligation survived Order42's confirmation. Duplicate delivery is possible at the next boundary.
messages.step.remaining.title: State the limits
messages.step.remaining.lead: The repair does not guarantee exactly-once delivery, consumer processing, broker ordering, immediate availability, or idempotent downstream effects.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer to account creation
messages.step.transfer.lead: An account is created, then a welcome-email request is queued. A crash between those actions leaves the account without a durable email obligation. Which facts should share a commit?
messages.step.recap.title: Six Questions recap
messages.step.recap.lead: A shared database transaction closes the confirmed-order-without-obligation gap. The broker remains separate, so relay publication can still be repeated.
